title: Quiet launch and rollback runway for batching/caching recommendations
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Implement a "quiet launch" workflow that safely applies Redwood Optimize batching and KV-cache recommendations with a reversible "rollback runway". The flow must combine simulated traffic, shadow (mirror) traffic, micro-canaries, and a staged operator approval window so we reduce token cost without risking customer latency or correctness regressions. Primary constraints: no user-facing latency degradation > 5% p95, no error-rate increases above 0.2%, and maintain per-route semantic fidelity (measured via prompt-level evals and regression alerts). The system should support: 1) preflight simulation harness using historical traces, 2) 1% mirrored traffic pilot with non-blocking telemetry only, 3) progressive increments (1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated gating, 4) a configurable rollback runway that keeps last-known-good configs and supports fast revert within a 10-minute SLO, 5) operator approval checkpoints with contextual diagnostics (heatmaps, recent diffs, PR links, affected routes), and 6) audit logging and canary-visible metrics persisted to the Console for postmortem. Deliverables: a coordinator service endpoint, a canary policy DSL, a lightweight operator UI in Console (pilot controls + approve/revert), telemetry gating rules, and a test suite with synthetic regressions.

Acceptance criteria: 
- End-to-end quiet launch flow exercised on internal test tenants with simulated regressions (latency spike, hallucination regression) and verified automatic halt.
- Rollback completes to a validated previous config within 10 minutes in 95% of simulated failures.
- Console surfaces canary heatmap and a single-click emergency revert.
- Audit records for every staged apply contain the suggestion id, operator id, metrics snapshot, and linked PR/Confluence doc.
comments: 2026-02-24 Aisha Kumar: Created ticket with initial design sketch. Preferred to avoid a global "blast" and rely on shadowing + micro-canary.

2026-02-26 Liam O'Neal: Spiked a prototype coordinator that accepts policy JSON and orchestrates mirrored traffic to a canary pool (branch: feature/quiet-launch). Found early thrash in KV cache priming under mirrored load — added a simulated priming step to plan.

2026-03-03 Brandon Lee (PM): Reviewed gating thresholds. Requested an explicit hallucination regression metric (normalized BLEU-style similarity + token divergence) included in the gate. Also wants per-customer opt-out available.
2026-03-05 Design review (Maya Chen): Console mockups for pilot controls posted in Confluence. Preference for a single 'Abort & Revert' action placed next to the canary heatmap.

2026-03-09 QA (Rosa Martínez): Wrote tests that inject 10% synthetic latency and verify gating stops promotion. Found one edge case where cached KV size exceeded expected bucket and caused OOM in a small canary node; added safety limiter to canary scheduler.

2026-03-12 Liam O'Neal: Implemented telemetry gate evaluation and the rollback runway store. Filed PR for coordinator (see link). Next: integrate operator UI and add audit chain entries with request token sampling. Planning demo on 2026-03-18 for SRE and Growth teams.
